target: Regular two-party U.S. Senate Republican margin minus strictly prior national presidential two-party margin
features: strictly prior presidential state lean versus national presidential margin
Prior regular same-seat six-year Senate margin adjusted for the national presidential election strictly before that Senate election
same-seat prior winner running again, signed by Republican or Democratic party
selection: Expanding-cycle margin mean-square error through 2018 only; candidate set from that election, prior presidential and Senate outcomes only
futureNationalInput: Dated national generic-ballot polling, converted to two-party margin; retain source clock
residualModel: Student-t with fixed4 degrees of freedom and RMS from expanding development residuals; at least10 margin-point standard deviation. Combine national polling RMS sensitivity in variance.
limitations: Historical feature clocks use strictly earlier election cycles, but revised final-result datasets and final nominee identities are not an original October forecast vintage.
A new current assessment may use dated stable historical returns and current polling; its observation clock never replaces component publication clocks.
Incumbency inference can miss replacements, appointments or name changes. Exclude cases with ambiguous or multi-candidate major-party identity.
Current win estimates are model assumptions, not calibrated confidence floors or guaranteed settlement payouts.
No contest order authority, no historical market profit proof and no changes to prior frozen cohorts.

Replacing prior national presidential returns with current generic-ballot polling is a scenario adjustment; Senate/presidential/House turnout and ticket splitting differ. Historical checks cannot prove its 2026 probability calibration.
amendmentReason: House dataset requires a Guestbook response. No personal response was submitted. Use only downloaded public Senate/presidential results, before fitting or selecting any model.
currentPollingTreatment: Forward scenario substitutes current national generic-ballot margin for the strictly prior national presidential margin. Transportability is an explicit model assumption, not a measured coefficient.
